messages.content: "Can you first find me a vegan, main course recipe that can be prepared within 30 minutes? After that, could you please retrieve the details of the scientific discovery of Gravity using the most accepted method? Once done, I would also like to know about the discovery of the Higgs Boson particle using the same method. Lastly, could you find me a gluten-free dessert recipe that can be prepared within 45 minutes?"

function.name: find_recipe
function.description: Find a recipe based on the dietary restrictions, recipe type, and time constraints. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

dietary_restrictions.description: Dietary restrictions e.g. vegan, vegetarian, gluten free, dairy free.

recipe_type.description: Type of the recipe. E.g. dessert, main course, breakfast.

time.description: Time limit in minutes to prep the meal.

function.name: science_history_get_discovery_details
function.description: Retrieve the details of a scientific discovery based on the discovery name. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

discovery.description: The name of the discovery, e.g. Gravity

method_used.description: The method used for the discovery, default value is 'default' which gives the most accepted method.

message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions sequentially:

1) find_recipe with dietary_restrictions="vegan", recipe_type="main course", time=30.

2) science_history_get_discovery_details with discovery="Gravity", method_used unspecified (most accepted). So we pass only "gravity".

But note: The tool expects discovery as string; case-insensitive maybe but use exactly "Gravity". Provide no method or set method_used='default'.

Then third request: get discovery details for "Higgs Boson particle" using same method. Use discovery param accordingly.

Fourth request: find_recipe again with dietary_restrictions="gluten-free", recipe_type="dessert", time=45.

Thus four calls. We should output each result separately. We'll do them one after another. Let's produce JSON responses from each function. Then combine into assistant response. Probably best to separate results clearly. We'll just return combined text summarizing all. But instructions say "Once done ... I'd also like to know ..." so likely want step-by-step outputs. I'll provide each answer separated by headings.
